arxiv-1904-07387.title: Predicting Fluid Intelligence of Children using T1-weighted MR Images and a StackNet
arxiv-1904-07387.creator: Po-Yu Kao, Angela Zhang, Michael Goebel, Jefferson W. Chen, B.S. Manjunath
arxiv-1904-07387.description: Abstract In this work, we utilize T1-weighted MR images and StackNet to predict fluid intelligence in adolescents. Our framework includes feature extraction, feature normalization, feature denoising, feature selection, training a StackNet, and predicting fluid intelligence. The extracted feature is the distribution of different brain tissues in different brain parcellation regions. The proposed StackNet consists of three layers and 11 models.

arxiv-2102-11383.title: A Generalized Eulerian-Lagrangian Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Transport Problems Thanks: Research of the first author is supported by the China Scholarship Council for 2 years’ study at the University of Delaware. Research of the second author is supported by NSF grant NSF-DMS-1818924, Air For
arxiv-2102-11383.creator: Xue Hong, Jing-Mei Qiu
arxiv-2102-11383.description: Abstract We propose a generalized Eulerian-Lagrangian (GEL) discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method. The method is a generalization of the Eulerian-Lagrangian (EL) DG method for transport problems proposed in [arXiv preprint arXiv: 2002.02930 (2020)], which tracks solution along approximations to characteristics in the DG framework, allowing extra large time stepping size with stability.

arxiv-2104-09443.title: Numerical analysis of a Neumann boundary control problem with a stochastic parabolic equation
arxiv-2104-09443.creator: Qin Zhou, Binjie Li
arxiv-2104-09443.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qin Zhou, Binjie Li. This paper analyzes the discretization of a Neumann boundary control problem with a stochastic parabolic equation, where an additive noise occurs in the Neumann boundary condition. The convergence is established for general filtration, and the convergence rate O ⁡ ( τ 1 / 4 − ϵ + h 1 / 2 − ϵ ) O(\tau^{1/4-\epsilon}+h^{1/2-\epsilon}) is derived for the natural filtration of the Q Q -Wiener process.

arxiv-2106-08253.title: A Syntax-Guided Edit Decoder for Neural Program Repair Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3468264.3468544 fse21main-p92-p ISBN: 978-1-4503-8562-6/21/08 Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering; August 23–28
arxiv-2106-08253.creator: Qihao Zhu, Zeyu Sun, Yuan-an Xiao, Wenjie Zhang, Kang Yuan, Yingfei Xiong, Lu Zhang
arxiv-2106-08253.description: Abstract . Automated Program Repair (APR) helps improve the efficiency of software development and maintenance. Recent APR techniques use deep learning, particularly the encoder-decoder architecture, to generate patches. Though existing DL-based APR approaches have proposed different encoder architectures, the decoder remains to be the standard one, which generates a sequence of tokens one by one to replace the faulty statement.

arxiv-2107-05783.title: Non-Visual Cooking: Exploring Practices and Challenges of Meal Preparation by People with Visual Impairments Conference: The 23rd International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility; October 18–22, 2021; Virtual Event, USA The 23rd International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computer
arxiv-2107-05783.creator: Franklin Mingzhe Li, Jamie Dorst, Peter Cederberg, Patrick Carrington
arxiv-2107-05783.description: Abstract . The reliance on vision for tasks related to cooking and eating healthy can present barriers to cooking for oneself and achieving proper nutrition. There has been little research exploring cooking practices and challenges faced by people with visual impairments.

arxiv-2108-07625.title: Hybrid dynamical type theories for navigation Thanks: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible.
arxiv-2108-07625.creator: Paul Gustafson, Jared Culbertson, Daniel Koditschek
arxiv-2108-07625.description: Abstract We present a hybrid dynamical type theory equipped with useful primitives for organizing and proving safety of navigational control algorithms. This type theory combines the framework of Fu–Kishida–Selinger for constructing linear dependent type theories from state-parameter fibrations with previous work on categories of hybrid systems under sequential composition.

arxiv-2108-10184.title: Constraints on compact binary merger evolution from spin-orbit misalignment in gravitational-wave observations 2021 Constraints on compact binary merger evolution from spin-orbit misalignment in gravitational-wave observations – References
arxiv-2108-10184.creator: B. P. Gompertz, M. Nicholl, P. Schmidt, G. Pratten, A. Vecchio
arxiv-2108-10184.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by B. P. Gompertz, M. Nicholl, P. Schmidt, G. Pratten, A. Vecchio. The identification of the first confirmed neutron star - black hole (NS-BH) binary mergers by the LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA collaboration provides the opportunity to investigate the properties of the early sample of confirmed and candidate events. Here, we focus primarily on the tilt angle of the black hole’s spin relative to the orbital angular momentum vector of the binary, and the implications for the physical processes that determine this tilt.

arxiv-2309-09105.title: Distinguishable consequence of classical gravity on quantum matter
arxiv-2309-09105.creator: Serhii Kryhin, Vivishek Sudhir
arxiv-2309-09105.description: Abstract What if gravity is classical? If true, a consistent co-existence of classical gravity and quantum matter requires that gravity exhibit irreducible fluctuations. These fluctuations can mediate classical correlations, but not quantum entanglement, between the quantized motion of the gravitationally interacting matter.

arxiv-2412-10225.title: Tight contact structures on toroidal plumbed 3-manifolds Thanks: Subjclass[2020] : 57K10, 57K14, 57K33
arxiv-2412-10225.creator: Tanushree Shah, Jonathan Simone
arxiv-2412-10225.description: Abstract . We consider tight contact structures on plumbed 3-manifolds with no bad vertices. We discuss how one can count the number of tight contact structures with zero Giroux torsion on such 3-manifolds and explore conditions under which Giroux torsion can be added to these tight contact structures without making them overtwisted.

arxiv-2509-03192.title: Oscillons and bubbles in Q Q -ball dynamics
arxiv-2509-03192.creator: D. Canillas Martínez, P. Dorey, T. Romańczukiewicz, Paul M. Saffin, K. Sławińska, A. Wereszczyński
arxiv-2509-03192.description: Abstract We show that, in the thin-wall regime, Q Q -ball–anti- Q Q -ball collisions reveal chaotic behaviour. This is explained by the resonant energy transfer mechanism triggered by the internal modes hosted by the Q Q -balls and by the existence of ephemeral states, that is unstable, sometimes even short-lived, field configurations that appear as intermediate states.

pmc-10578175.title: Visual Field Progression After Glaucoma Surgery in Pseudoexfoliation versus Primary Glaucoma
pmc-10578175.creator: Aparna Rao, Rakhi P D’Cruz
pmc-10578175.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). PurposeTo compare visual field progression in severity-matched pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (XFG) and primary glaucoma after intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction by filtering surgery.MethodsPatients with XFG (n=32), primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG, n=33) or primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG, n=28) that underwent routine cataract and glaucoma filtering surgery by the same surgeon (APR) between May 2017 and September 2021, were included for this prospective study. Rate of progression (ROP) was determined using guided progression analysis and compared between XFG and primary glaucoma.

pmc-10662515.title: Acute myocardial infarction diagnosed in emergency departments: a report from the National Emergency Department Information System (NEDIS) of Korea, 2018–2022
pmc-10662515.creator: Shin Ahn, Eunsil Ko, Young Sun Ro
pmc-10662515.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). mprehensive analysis of the changing trends in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) presentations at emergency departments (EDs) across the nation. In this study, utilizing data from the National Emergency Department Information System (NEDIS), we aim to provide an overview of the current status of AMI diagnosed in EDs in Korea, including trends in incidence, demographic characteristics, and clinical outcomes categorized by age group and ED category. AMI diagnosis was confirmed using diagnostic codes I210–I219 during the 2018–2022 study period.

pmc-11327248.title: Retinal microvascular changes in patients with pancreatitis and their clinical significance
pmc-11327248.creator: Yun-Qing Luo, Zi-Song Xu, Jin-Yu Hu, Qian-Min Ge, Jie Zou, Hong Wei, Xian-Mei Zhou, Xuan Liao, Qian Ling, Liang-Qi He, Cheng Chen, Xiao-Yu Wang, Yan-Mei Zeng, Yi Shao
pmc-11327248.description: Acute pancreatitis, a common exocrine inflammatory disease affecting the pancreas, is characterized by intense abdominal pain and multiple organ dysfunction. However, the alterations in retinal blood vessels among individuals with acute pancreatitis remain poorly understood. This study employed optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) to examine the superficial and deep retinal blood vessels in patients with pancreatitis.

pmc-11459998.title: A diagnosis that’s hard to swallow: case report of delayed onset lateral medullary syndrome presenting with only dysphagia
pmc-11459998.creator: Jose Ernesto Gomez, Eric Justin Ho
pmc-11459998.description: BackgroundLateral Medullary Syndrome (LMS) is a posterior circulation stroke (PCS) that has a broad array of manifestations but most classically presents with Horner’s syndrome, ipsilateral ataxia, and ipsilateral hyperalgesia. Although dysphagia is also common, isolated and single presentation of this alone is rare and there are only a few case reports of this in the literature.

pmc-11651945.title: A novel nephrometry scoring system outperforms RENAL score, PADUA score, and SPARE score for feasibility prediction of nephron-sparing surgery in children with bilateral Wilms tumor
pmc-11651945.creator: Zonghan Li, Jiayi Li, Ning Sun, Qifeng Zhang, Weiping Zhang, Zhenwu Li, Hongcheng Song
pmc-11651945.description: BackgroundSeveral nephrometry scores have been proposed and applied in the adult population. We previously established a novel model to predict the feasibility of nephron-sparing surgery (NSS) in pediatric bilateral Wilms tumor (WT) patients. This study aimed to evaluate whether our model had better predictive performance compared to other scores.MethodsData from 58 patients during the period 2008–2019 were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-11690630.title: HOME HEALTH CARE USE AND OUTCOMES AMONG PERSONS WITH DEMENTIA: A SCOPING REVIEW
pmc-11690630.creator: Jamie Smith, Julia Burgdorf, Tiffany Riser, Miriam Ryvicker
pmc-11690630.description: One-third of home healthcare (HHC) recipients are persons living with dementia (PLWD). HHC provides skilled nursing and therapy delivered in the patient’s home. Amid population aging and a shift towards home- and community-based care, there is a growing need for HHC services for PLWD. However, dementia care research has historically focused on institutional care settings, and HHC has been understudied.

pmc-11710549.title: Vitamin D and donepezil intervention in ovariectomized rats: modulating neuroinflammation in the aging brain
pmc-11710549.creator: Lucineia Danielski, Eduarda Behenck Medeiros, Gabriela Piovesan Fenilli, Gabriel Casagrande Zabot, Adrielly Vargas, Amanda L Boaventura, Mariana Cardoso Lumertz, Franciane Bobinski, Vijayasree V Giridharan, Tatiana Barichello, Josiane Budni
pmc-11710549.description: BackgroundAging is a natural, irreversible process that can be successful or pathological, resulting in chronic degenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Low levels of estrogen characterize menopause. Research reveals that the lack of these hormones may be related to dementia and that vitamin D (vit D), when supplemented, has a neuroprotective and neuromodulator effect.

pmc-13411974.title: Design and validation of revised medication assessment tool for community-acquired Pneumonia: rMAT-CAP
pmc-13411974.creator: Sahar Elnajjar, Sabariah Noor Harun, Semira Beshir, Ali Qureshi, Dujana Al Hamed, Hebah Al Jaghoub, Hamzeh Al Subbah, Danish Khowaja
pmc-13411974.description: BackgroundEvaluating therapeutic appropriateness is a cornerstone of antimicrobial stewardship. The original Medication Assessment Tool for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (MAT-CAP), developed in Norway, requires adaptation to account for evolving IDSA/ATS recommendations and region-specific antimicrobial resistance patterns in the UAE. To revise, adapt, and validate a Medication Assessment Tool for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (rMAT-CAP), adapted to the UAE healthcare context.

pmc-13473941.title: From local validation to global standardization of three-dimensional printing in radiotherapy☆
pmc-13473941.creator: José Vedelago, Christina Stengl, Barbara Knäusl

pmc-13485962.title: Triglyceride–glucose index and hyperhomocysteinemia within a cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic biomarker network: insights from interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling
pmc-13485962.creator: Hongzhou Liu, Ru Wang, Huadan Zhu, Chuan Song, Li Shi, Manka Zhang, Song Dong, Shuangtong Yan
pmc-13485962.description: BackgroundAlthough the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index is an established surrogate marker of insulin resistance and metabolic burden, its relationship with hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) within the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) framework remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG and HHcy and to prioritize CKM-related biomarkers using interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling.

pmc-13594189.title: Ventral tegmental area glutamatergic neurons suppress hippocampal ripples and induce head movements in mice
pmc-13594189.creator: Manivannan Subramaniyan, Sumithrra Manivannan, Maggie S. Zhou, John A. Dani
pmc-13594189.description: Ripples are brief, high-frequency hippocampal oscillations crucial for memory consolidation, occurring predominantly during non-rapid-eye-movement (NREM) sleep. While ripples are generated intrinsically within the hippocampus, growing evidence suggests that their occurrence is modulated by subcortical regions. Whether the ventral tegmental area (VTA)—a subcortical region that directly projects to the hippocampus—regulates ripple activity remains unknown.
